utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, doctor. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we need the side screens? Good morning, Mr. Saxon. The processes of ensuring that the witness has full protective measures have a delayed us in greeting. Please, if you would continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. At this time I would like the assistance of the usher to place this piece of paper with the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, witness, I don't want you to state your true name, but do you see your true name on that piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there's some other information on that piece of paper in front of you. Is that information accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, the information are accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could that piece of paper be shown to the -- sorry. If that piece of paper can be shown to the Defence counsel. And, Your Honours, if there's no objection, then I would seek to tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon, it will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be exhibit number P370, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I heard marked for identification from the court officer. But I heard it will be received from His Honour and I'm not quite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So this will be exhibit number 370, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not going to address you by your true name today. I'm going to address by the pseudonym M-171, or I may say Witness 171, can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And can we also agree, I will try to speak slowly to you and ask you hopefully what will be short and simple answers and can you try to speak slowly as well into the microphone and provide me with reasonably short and simple responses to assist the interpreters. Can we do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness 171.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic and together with my colleague Guenael Mettraux we appear for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I start asking the questions, Mrs. M-171, I will ask you to pause a bit after I have asked you the question that you should understand in my language and wait until it is interpreted and after that, answer the question that I have asked. I will also pause, wait for the translation of your answer, since the questions and the answers must be interpreted for Their Honours and the other colleagues in the courtroom to be able to know what we are discussing. Did you understood these plea I made to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to move into a private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in Macedonia --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in Macedonia, there was a conflict between the sabotage terrorist groups and the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, the army and the police. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The competent bodies of the Republic of Macedonia have made a decision establishing that the city general hospital in Skopje is the hospital where the Albanians victims of the conflict would be treated. Is that fact correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the treatment of the Albanian population that was injured in relation to the conflict, you also -- the hospital actually, also continued to carry out its regular task for the civilian population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers of the army of the Republic of Macedonia and the police members who were injured in the conflict were mainly treated in the military hospital in Skopje. Is that fact correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally do not know or do you know the reasons that made the competent bodies issue such a decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: I suppose it was due to security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "security reasons," could you agree with me if I were to say that those security reasons were mainly protection of patients because the treatment at a single facility of both the persons injured in the conflict, persons in the conflict who belonged to different sides in the conflict could lead to conflicts within the hospitals, between the actual patients or their relatives. Is that generally your opinion when you say "due to security reasons"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, that decision was sound, reasonable; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask to move into a private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You answered various questions of my colleagues relating to the way patients are usually admitted in the general city hospital in Skopje. Apart from their regular duties, the doctors in the hospital, as you say, are part of duty teams considering the fact that the injuries that the patients who are (redacted) have require for a team of doctors to be present in the hospital at all times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the hospital, even prior to the conflict, during the conflict and after the conflict, always has a team of duty doctors who have to be there in the hospital in case of emergencies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that at that time, the practice, the general practice was for a patient who came to the hospital to have a medical file, a record opened. This is a file that on the cover page has a title the history of illness or the case history; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this medical record, you write down the basic data of the patient, the anamnesis, information if the patient is referred to further treatment or analysis, laboratory analysis, for example, as well as other decisions that the doctor who admitted the patient deems necessary for the just therapy of the patient to be confirmed. Is this all of the information that is contained in this medical record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This medical record that is compiled in the hospital also contains the results of all the analysis that had been ordered or carried out by specialists; that is to say, by laboratory staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This record also contains proposed therapy, the way it should be administered to the patient, and in case the patient remains in the hospital, the everyday condition of the patient, it's also recorded in this medical record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the patient is discharged, a discharge paper is composed, which also contains a diagnosis and further treatment for that patient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The doctor that admits the patient, upon receiving the preliminary results of the analysis, he refers the patient further, whether to intensive care or to home treatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This procedure is carried out at all times, regardless of whether it is a time of conflict or peace; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This procedure and the way of filling out a medical record goes for every patient, regardless of who that person in question is; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: National, religious, or any other affiliation is not a basis or a reason for any of the information in the medical record --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the last part of the answer, thank you. The question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As I was asked to repeat my question, I will. Is it correct that neither national or religious affiliation or any other affiliation of the person received as a patient is not a basis for any information to be filled out in the medical record. The only basis for putting the data in the medical record are only of medical nature; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering your long experience as a (redacted) (redacted), could you confirm for us that this is the way how work was carried out in this hospital throughout your professional engagement and that this practice has never changed, even during the conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, (redacted) and other medical staff treated all patients equally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, totally professionally.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) otherwise, and you also have never heard any patient to complain about the work of your colleagues; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair for me to conclude that in your hospital, in the treatment of patients there was no discrimination. Patients were treated on basis of medical indication and the need to administer them help; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: In our hospital, before, during and after the event and nowadays, we work very professionally and the interest is of our main interest at all times [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the conflict in 2001, (redacted), and the hospital you worked in, cooperated with the international Red Cross committee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that nobody from the ICRC or the Red Cross of the Republic of Macedonia has ever complained about the work of the doctors or the way they treat their patients?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001 more persons who had sustained injuries in relation to the conflict were brought to your hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. During that year, during the conflict, more persons were brought in our hospital. The number is quite large, but I don't know the exact number. The majority of them were citizens of Kosovo. Their situation varied from light to serious injuries. Many -- of many of them we saved their lives and they were released from hospital in a very good condition.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some of these persons had injuries sustained by fire-arm but there were also persons who had other types of injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my colleague asked you about the injuries that are recorded in the medical record of the patient, the record that you were shown, you answered, stating the following: That these injuries could be sustained -- excuse me, I will reformulate my question. When answering the question of my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, whether the content of the medical record is correct, and it corresponds to the situation that you saw with that patient, you said, yes, and then you explained why you thought it was correct, what the patient told you about the way he was injured. My question is the following. Did you, before or after admitting these patients that you were asked about, see any other persons who were injured by mechanical instruments during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will probably agree with me that these injuries could be inflicted also in offering resistance to persons who took part in a given conflict; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my colleague asked you where this medical record can be found, if I understood you correctly, you said that this file is kept separately in the documentation, scientific documentation unit. Did I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to clarify this. First of all, tell me, is it correct that the medical record or file of the patient is updated throughout the time he is in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this record, the doctors put in all the information about the steps they have undertaken in treating this particular patient; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a patient is discharged from hospital, is it correct that this medical record continues to be kept in your documentation, in case it is necessary for that patient to came later on for visits, for checkups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. We keep the records for approximately 15 years and then we destroy them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the doctor is able to see that documentation only when a certain patient comes -- revisits the hospital and only if it is necessary for that patient to continue a certain therapy or to consult the doctor for the medical treatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understand well, only when there is no need anymore for further treatment of a given patient, it is at that time that these documents are put in this research documentation as you said; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: The patients are sent to the -- to the room where the research documentation is kept. These documents are sent there when he is discharged from the hospital and when his treatment has ended.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These documents, if I can suggest, are not anymore under the control of the doctor but they are under the control of the administration of the hospital; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And may I say that access to this documentation is allowed only to the administration of the hospital, respectively to the medical staff that would ask for such -- for these documents if they need any information in relation to a treatment of a patient; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. But in some cases, access can also be given to the court based on some procedure and if such access is requested by the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was my following question. Therefore, access to this medical documentation and to this information, the hospital must give such an access also upon the request of a court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. And this occurs very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, the court can also request for expertise of some illnesses or injuries and you very often appear before a court in the capacity of experts to clarify the seriousness of the illness; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. We very often issue a medical certificate or we compile medical reports upon the request of the court, and also in the (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, madam M-171, that in case of suspicion that a given illness or injury could be a result of a criminal act, then all the organs and the hospital itself are required to inform the competent judge or investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. This procedure is conducted regularly, when there are some violent injuries, death from unknown cause, accident, fights, murders and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. I didn't get the beginning of the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the question because we didn't have the microphone before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I think I spoke very quickly and I will make the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, is it correct, Madam M-171, that information on such cases was provided to the Prosecutor or the Judge by the hospital administration, director or deputy director, i.e. the hospital management?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the examination the Prosecution has shown you a document which can be found in tab number 6. This is P54, which represents the notes that have been prepared in the city hospital by the investigating judge, Velce Pancevski. Do you recall that when the Prosecutor showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, this demonstrates that the investigating judge was there in the hospital himself and that the director or someone on his behalf gave the judge all the data in relation to the injured persons that were in the hospital. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. There is usually done immediately after the admittance of a patient.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that the description of the injuries that were recorded in these notes of the judge are exactly the same as the one you recall that were sustained by the patient when he was admitted. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that since the investigating judge was informed directly by the administration of the hospital on everything that is relevant for the job, for the work of the investigating judge, it was not necessary for you to inform the Prosecutor or the investigating judge about that again. Would this be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, this would be correct, because with that, the procedure has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe -- Your Honours, maybe it would be a good time now to make break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Public. Oh, we are in public. We need to have our first break at this point, and we will resume at 11.00. And the court officer will -- if I could ask the witness to stay where she is for the moment, the court officer will make the physical arrangements for to you leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I proceed with the cross-examination, I would like to ask for assistance from the usher to distribute the binders that -- with the documents that I will be using with the witness. We have a sufficient number of copies for the Bench and for the Prosecution and for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Madam M-171, before the break, we were speaking about the access to the medical record to other persons. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in order to complete my questions in reference to this issue, I'd like to ask you whether it is correct that doctors in the medical record of the patient enter precisely and accurately all the results that they receive from lab tests, from X-rays, or all other specialist tests that are conducted in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Neither you nor your colleagues have ever entered in the medical record those results that have not come out from lab test results or from X-rays or other specialist tests; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to go now to private session, because the name written in the documents could reveal the identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You had decided this in the past as well, but I had simply forgotten that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before this Court, Witness 171, testified Mr. Ismail Ramadani. I would like now to ask you to look at the first page which is on the page 998 of the transcript, line 23. The witness was shown this medical report. And as you can see, the question was that is a medical report from the general hospital Skopje [In English] on the upper part. [Interpretation] And the answer was, yes, it's here. Now I would like you ask you to turn the next page. I apologise, this document is in tab 4, and this is an excerpt from the testifying of Mr. Ismail Ramadani. Now we are on page 999, on line 16. The question was "[In English] You were admitted on the 13th of August, 2001." The answer was yes "[In English], that's correct." The question was, again in the English, "[In English] mention there that you had a serious fracture of the 2nd to 8th ribs on your left side and fracture of the 7th, 8th and 10th ribs on your right side. My question is: Is the description of your injuries correct?" [Interpretation] The answer was: "You meant if it is correct, no, I wouldn't say so. I had more ribs that were broken and here it is mentioned only a few." [Interpretation] My question, Madam 171, is, again, whether in this medical report -- whether this medical report in an objective way points out all the injuries that were sustained by this patient?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, all the injuries are recorded accurately, and there are also X-rays that confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the statement of this witness on the way the injuries were recorded, in your opinion, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, the statement is not correct, is untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you to look at the page 1026. This is the same witness, and on line 19, the question says: "[In English] You were rendered adequate medical care; is that correct?" [Interpretation] Answer says: "[In English] Macedonian forces ill treat us, even at the hospital. They made us take off our civilian clothes and they put the pyjama on us. They ill treated us and then after that they sent us to the room." [Interpretation] The question says: "[In English] Offered you appropriate medical care; is that correct?" [Interpretation] The answer: "[In English] The doctors gave us only treatment and then tied our wounds, the wounds that we had on our heads and faces, only that, nothing else." [Interpretation] Question says: "[In English] That my learned colleague has shown you it is stated that you were administered all necessary medication, then this would not be correct, correctly written; is that correct?" [Interpretation] This is not correct. I told here a little bit before they only gave us IV treatment, two bottles of medication and then the following day, on the 13th of August, a new bottle of IV medication. [Interpretation] "I don't know what IV medication means. "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... For, they gave us a treatment, applied a cream on our wounds, and one of the doctors said that you can't feel immediately, so you need several application on this cream." [Interpretation] Could you tell me, please, Mrs. M-171, in your deep conviction and from what you saw from the medical documentation is it correct that each of the patients admitted were administered the therapy that corresponded to their situation and their injuries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. And I can explain it. First, at the admission of the patients, the usual protocol for admission of patients in our hospital was followed, that is, anamnesis was taken, an examination was conducted, they were sent to diagnostic procedure, the laboratory tests were taken and X-rays were made. After that, they were again admitted in the doctor's office and records were made of the admission. The patients were admitted as the documents previously shown to us stated. They were received in the shock ward. That is near the intensive care but this is not a room where the severely injured patients are admitted. It is rather a room where they are taken for observation and depending on their status, health status, they are further transferred to other wards. That shock room, shock ward, usually has anaesthesiologists working in it and these patients as well as any patients before the conflict, during the conflict, or after the conflict are administered therapy and in the medical history that was shown to me before now, I saw the note written by an anaesthesiologist where the standard therapy for such type of injuries was administered. It is correct that, as the patient said, it is IV therapy that is usually administered in such type of injuries, then serum anti-tetanus, because there were wounds that were still not treated, then analgetics and antibiotics, and nothing further is administered to any patient with such or similar injuries. This is it standard therapy and we have followed certain medical protocols. Furthermore, since the patient had good general health status, he was transferred to the trauma ward where the therapy continued. With regards to the treatment of the wounds. They were standard. As the standard procedure is an ointment for standard treatment was administered and they were then bandaged or they were left for an open treatment, then again ointment was put on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So thank you very much, which means that the treatment corresponded to the status of the injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And such treatment would be administered regardless of the time and regardless of the person of the patient whenever the injuries would be of that nature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There is no difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me when the patient is sent to intensive care, is it correct that it is medical staff admitting him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, medical staff employed in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Medical staff give them that clothes that they will wear during their stay in the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They are undressed at admission and they wear with the standard pyjamas, as it was done with these patients.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there was no other party, third party in the hospital other than medical staff could treat the patients, provide them medical care. It is only the medical staff that does that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. We have janitors there and we have security so no one else could climb up to the shock ward and the intensive care ward.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you were at the hospital at that time, is it correct that you did not see any person, and particularly not policemen, ill treating the patients admit in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: This is not the case. Such case has never happened at our facility, not only with regards to these patients. It had never happened before or after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Mrs. M-171, that the allegations made by the witness before this Court about the ill-treatment in the hospital and the medical treatment that they were rendered are simply inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: The allegations of the witness are not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you now to look in the same tab, the page number 1.073.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 1.083.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness, Osman Ramadani, who has testified before this Court, in line 21 to 25 on that page, and then it continues for further two lines on the next page, has testified in the following way. The question was: "[In English] Is it correct that you were given an appropriate medical assistance, you been operated and then you remain in the hospital until you recovered?" [Interpretation] And the answer was: "[In English] That's not correct. They did what they wanted with me. I witnessed torture there as well. I was hit there too. I don't know who hit me. I was hit and beaten up in the hospital as well. They kept me there as long as they wanted, two or three days. There were no rules." [Interpretation] Considering your previous answer, could you tell me whether this statement of this witness about the treatment received in the hospital is simply inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an absolute lie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Unless it can be established that this witness treated Mr. Osman Ramadani and/or was with Mr. Osman Ramadani during the entire time that Mr. Ramadani was in the hospital, I'm not sure how this witness can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, in some respects that may well be correct. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think you really need to spend the time going through each (redacted), if you can get were her a general assurance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. And in accordance with your instruction (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) So I kindly ask that it is redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I've just attended to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to you look at the document in tab 2, P22, and considering that the name of the protected witness is mentioned, this document should not be displayed to the general public. Mrs. M-171, you can recognise from this document as well that you were the person who admitted this patient; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that this patient as well was treated in the same way? According to the procedure, medical treatment was ordered and medical care was given, such as his medical status required?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If this witness has asserted before this Court that he was beaten not only by the policemen but also by the nurses and doctors, what would you say to such testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: This is a falsity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab number 16, and before that, I would like to ask you the following: In your hospital, apart from doctors and medical staff, are there also medical staff and doctors who are not Macedonians by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. There are doctors from all ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the situation was such in 2001 as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the situation is such even today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Has any of your Albanian colleagues told you at any time during 2001 that they were witnesses or that they have heard complaints about ill-treatment of the persons brought from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in tab 6 and not 16, as the transcript reads.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. M-171, you see now a letter in the upper left-hand corner. It states it is a letter sent by the public health institution, specialist surgery hospital Sv. Naum Ohridski. That is 65 ter 1D453, Macedonian pages 1D4187, while the English page is 1D4188. Can you see in the upper left corner the name and the address of the hospital issuing the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the hospital where you are employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is signed by Dr. Nikola Gruev; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel, please. Could the counsel please repeat the entire question. We haven't heard the first part of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been warned to repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the explanation, can you see that this was a person who had been a director between 2000 and 2003. Is that the capacity of a director of the clinic that you mentioned when answered the questions of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this letter, Dr. Nikola Gruev answers to the request of the defence in relation to some issues of interest (redacted) (redacted). And among other things it states: "The specialist surgery hospital is an institution with 45 years of experience in treating surgical diseases. Specialist surgery hospital is a teaching centre for the Skopje medical faculty. Specialist surgery hospital personnel are of mixed ethnicity as well as the -- and the equipment can provide modern surgical treatment responding to urgent surgical needs and also elective surgery." It further states, "The admittance and treatment of patients, in the specialist surgery hospital has been solely based on their medical requirements, regardless of the ethnic or religious affiliation of the patient. "During the armed conflict in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001, the aforementioned principles were fully respected in the operation of the clinic. It can be seen also from the number of patients hospitalised or treated from an outpatient surgery, in 2001 the admission and treatment of all patients was performed solely on the basis of the medical symptoms for treatment and surgery regardless of the ethnic or religious affiliations. "The quality and performance of the tasks by the personnel in that clinic was observed by the International Red Cross and other domestic and foreign organisations that have visited the specialist surgery hospital. During this time, in 2001, we had not -- I as a director of the clinic had not received any complaints from individuals or national legal entities or their representatives or other institutions or organisations in relation to the treatment, medical or otherwise, of patients hospitalised in 2001." So my question is, Mrs. M-171, do you recognise this document as a document issued by your hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: This is a document I see for the first time. But because it has the official seal and the signature of the former director, that is (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection and the practice in this hospital, tell me whether the facts noted in this document are accurate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Facts noted in this document are absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, line 48, 13, "to the best of your knowledge," instead of "to the best of your recollection."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Really, a comment about procedure, although this is being tendered as a document from the hospital or a letter from Dr. Nikola Gruev, in many ways it is quite similar to a statement, a witness statement. The contents have been read into the record. I believe it was the practice established by the Chamber early on that certainly witness statements used during cross-examination would not be admitted, and I'm wondering whether it is necessary to admit this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We agree with Mr. Saxon, Ms. Residovic. You -- the essence of what you want from this document is clearly now included in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 7. That is 65 ter 1D454. 1D454, Macedonian page is 1D4189, and the English is 1D4190. Mrs. M-171, can you see again in the upper left corner the name of your hospital and the date this document was issued, 14th of April, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see the signature and the name of the acting director of the hospital, Mr. Viktor Kamilovski. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This document is a classical document issued by the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as you can see from the data about the hospital and the date of issuance, this document was addressed to Mr. Dragan Godzo upon his request as a member of the defence team of Mr. Ljube Boskoski. It cannot be read from the document, but the Court is aware that he is a member of the Defence team. Subject is report and the document reads follows: "The specialist surgery hospital Sv. Naum Ohridski, Skopje, a legal successor of the city general hospital clinical surgery hospital Sv. Naum Ohridski, Skopje, informs you about the following. The patients at the hospital are treated solely based on the medical indications regardless of the national ethnic or religious affiliation. There are no special statistics kept in the hospital about the number of patients according to their ethnic affiliation. If you would require such data for 2001 and 2006, we would need to -- for such data to be extracted from the medical records of all patients who were treated in the aforementioned period. Personnel in the hospital belongs to different ethnic and religious groups. "In 2006, out of the total of 340 employees, 306 were Macedonians, while there were 34 members of other ethnic groups. In 2001, out of a total of 237 Macedonians, 220 are Macedonians while there are 17 members of other ethnic communities. All the employees in the hospital carry out their duties in full, day shift, night shift, duty shifts, without any influence on that from their ethnic or religious affiliation." First of all, I would like to ask you, Mrs. M-171, are the data in this document accurate regarding the facts personally known to you as an employee of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: I suppose they are accurate, and that the data were derived from the files of the personnel service, so they must be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, although the contents of the document and the answer of the witness were recorded in the transcript, considering that this is an official document of the hospital, I would seek to tender it into evidence officially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, do you see any difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Prosecution does not see any significant difference between the form of this document and the previous document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber, Ms. Residovic, is concerned to keep unnecessary documents out of the written record, which is already a very large written record, because we have to be aware of all of them at the end of the trial. Where, in accordance with the standard practice of this Tribunal, in cross-examination a document is referred to and the material parts of it are reflected in the transcript, it is really unnecessary for any purpose that the document also be included as an exhibit, because we have in the transcript its material parts recorded and we have the witness's reaction to the contents of the document. I mention that just to remind you why it is for the last document and now for this document we would take the view that it is really unnecessary for this document to become an actual exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully understand the reasons that you explain. However, the Defence thinks that these are official documents of the hospital that this witness confirmed, and these documents prove an absolutely different situation in the hospital compared to the situation presented by the witnesses we've heard. Considering the fact that this witness confirmed this different situation, I believe that these official documents would help the Trial Chamber in giving weight to the statements and testimonies of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We have given our ruling. We do not see that the document, in addition to the transcripts which reveals that -- the nature of the document and its content, is of any value. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would kindly ask you to answer to some questions that I have and that I think you can answer considering your professional experience as a surgeon. First of all, please tell me is it correct that in your work you have come across injuries in the area of the abdomen and that were inflicted by fire-arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in general, these injuries are not deadly, but are serious and can lead to death unless medical treatment is administered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in case the adequate medical treatment is not administered, the patient, due to bleeding will die after a given period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Except for injuries of the aorta, this period through which the person who has sustained injuries to the abdomen, this person can live up to several hours to several days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes. If a blood vessel, which in the case of abdomen injuries is the aorta, it can lead to death, if there is other injuries, when we speak about intestines then the survival can be of several days and usually they could not die out of haemorrhaging but due to infection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to look at the document in tab 10. This is exhibit 1D78. So exhibit 1D78 represents the autopsy protocol that was done on April 9, 2003. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: You refer to the first page?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to the first page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The autopsy protocol is composed -- is prepared either immediately after the death of the patient from which the hospital the court has request an autopsy or after the exhumation or due to other medical or legal reasons. Would this be an accurate description of the time when an autopsy is conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: First let me tell you, Madam 171, that before this Court we had Dr. Zlatko Jakovski who testified and in the introduction of this autopsy protocol he is one of the autopsy performers of the given patient, and I will not ask any questions concerning the autopsy protocol because everything that was relevant in reference to this issue, there was a witness that testified. However, I would like to ask to you look at the last page of this protocol. This is page 5 of the Macedonian version, this is N00-4210 and in the English version is also -- the English version is on page 3. We have now these versions on the screen as well. In the last paragraph, as you can see, changes have been established which were caused by a projectile from a fire-arm in the lower left third of the stomach, and the direction of this projectile has been established as well. Do you agree with me, M-171, that these would be an injury of the stomach with a fire-arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you to look at the pictures that are in tab 11, Exhibit 1D4. Then picture in tab 12. This is Exhibit P9. And the picture in tab 13, 65 ter 608, 05016266. We will wait for one of those pictures to appear on the screen. I would like to ask the secretary to display -- the registry, I'm sorry, to display one of the pictures, 1D4 and P --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is asking for the last number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first -- so this one is 1D4, and please could you show the Exhibit P9 at the same time as well. Thank you. Now we see also P9. My question, Mrs. M-171, is whether what you see in these pictures is a typical fire-arm injury on the stomach which has also been described in the autopsy protocol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, this is a typical fire-arm injury on the lower part -- left part of the stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My concern at least in this photograph the wound itself is covered with a bandage, and I don't understand how this witness can even make a comment as to what kind of typical injury or what kind of injury it is if she was not examined the body herself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the witness has answered the question, Mr. Saxon. That may be a matter for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness -- the witness also saw the picture in the binder 69 ter P608 0501-6266.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, we've ruled in your favour. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. M-171, having in mind your professional knowledge, experience -- and experience, in these kind of wounds would this be a wound that -- in which death could occur after several hours because of haemorrhage or possible infection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: If we look at the picture where there is no bandage, 608, and if we look from the front part of the stomach, (redacted) (redacted), however, and if we look at the picture 194 from the back, in accordance with my experience, and I will repeat I'm not a forensic, it is obvious that this is a fire-arm wound from the front to the rear part, to behind. Since the projectile moved towards that direction this would probably have caused an injury to the colon on the colon descendent on the left side or to those accompanying tissues that are -- that cover the colon. Therefore, the -- there might have been a haemorrhage but these haemorrhage would not have brought -- led to -- to a quick death. It should have taken several hours, if this was the point of your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have answered in accordance with your experience and knowledge, and now I will show you a few documents or statements that are related to the time of the death of the person in question. I would only like to ask you to give me your answer to my questions. Before this Court the witness Elmaz Jusufi testified. This is on the transcript page 418. This document is in tab 14 and to the question of the Presiding Judge saying "[In English] That was after he had been shot, was it?" [Interpretation] The answer was: "[In English] He asked for water we couldn't provide him water and then he died." [Interpretation] To the question: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... "in the photograph a bandage has been put around his wounds, around his stomach. Do you know who put the bandage on?"

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because there was a lot of blood coming out of the wound. I tied the belly with a piece of sheet." [Interpretation] Presiding Judge: "[In English] You did that, was your son still alive or had he died by then?"? [Interpretation] [No interpretation] "[In English] He died at the moment." In tab 15, the transcript line 15 the name of Elmaz is stated and it should say Xhevdet. The witness Elmaz Jusufi on page 588 of the transcript to the question saying "[In English] wounding your son died." [Interpretation] Answer: "I can't give you -- maybe after half an hour or 40 minutes, 25 minutes, I wouldn't be able to say. I knew it was -- it wasn't long after he was wounded, not more than, let's say, 40 minutes." [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask you to look at the document in binder -- I'm sorry, it is not in your binder but I would like to show you a document 65 ter 1D15, 1D0196, page -- and I would like for this document not to be shown to the public, because it is not excluded for this person to appear as a witness and he might request protective measures. 65 ter 1D15. 1D0196 is the first page. Mrs. M-171, the witness on this page has given a statement to the Prosecutor's investigator on the 29th of September, 2004. Now I'd like you to go to page 1D0198. This is the same 65 ter. The page is 65 ter 1D15 and the page is 1D0198. Item 5 of this statement, the third sentence says: "[In English] Because I felt safer there since the ground floor of my house is not visible from the road. After 9.00, I was out in the yard of my house and I could see the yard of my nephew's house. I was on the same level as mine. I called by mobile phone my relative Rami Jusufi to check how they are doing because I knew that his father is an invalid and his mother was also in the house. He asked me if I could help him because he was wounded. He told me that I should be careful if I would enter his house, saying they are all in the garage of my house." [Interpretation] The -- "[In English] Saw him again after [interpretation] ultimate sentence says: "[In English] How he is, he said he was not feeling good at all and hung up the phone." [Interpretation] Item 9 of the same page. Could you please scroll down. In the middle, the sentence starts with: "[In English] 11, meanwhile I call my relative Rami Jusufi for the third time on the phone and ask him where his wife and children were. He told me that they are in his sister's house. The name of his sister is Mybera." [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask you to look at the document 65 ter 1D12. The document is 1D0134. I would also like to ask you again not to show to the public this page because the person mentioned is on the witness list and might request protective measures. The person that you see on the screen gave a statement to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal on the 30th of August, 2001 and on 1st of September, 2001. And he spoke about the death of Rami Jusufi. Now I would like to ask registry to show page one of this statement, which is 1D -- page 3 of the statement number 1D0136. The last paragraph of this page, the interviewed person said the following: "[In English] In contact with the villagers by phone. I got information about five killed people, one of them six years old. One of the killed was called Rami Jusufi, and his father whose name I don't recall told me about the killing of Rami. Some 50 paramilitaries had come to the yard of his house and they had killed Rami by shooting him in the stomach. Rami himself called to our office that they asking for help and I tried to encourage him, saying that we would try to send some first aid as soon as possible. However, this was impossible." [Interpretation] Please turn the next page. "[In English] And he died early in the evening." [Interpretation] My question to you, (redacted) I apologise. Could this word please be redacted from the transcript. Mrs. M-171, you heard the statements of two witnesses who say that the death of Rami Jusufi occurred immediately or within 40 minutes maximum and two other persons saying that Rami Jusufi was alive for few more hours and the last witness says that he died earlier in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: (redacted), could you please tell me whether it was -- whether it is true that this person had lived for a longer period of time, as these two persons say, or do you think that death has occurred immediately, as the two other witnesses say?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It seems to the Prosecution that this question is asking this witness to speculate, and I use the word "speculate" perhaps as an understatement. This witness did not view the body, did not view the injured person, and I don't see how this could be helpful to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has already responded by the type of wound when she saw the photographs and she gave her opinion. She is -- she can give such an opinion as an expert about the time of the death of Rami Jusufi. This is an almost identical question, which is now related to the different times conveyed by different witnesses. I do not see any reason why she could -- cannot reply to this question. This is not a speculation. This is an expert opinion and this is something the Court will have to decide upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, it seems to the Prosecution that if any witness should have received this question it was the witness Dr. Jakovski who performed the autopsy on this particular victim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, the Chamber is persuaded that it is not at all fair to the witness nor could any answer be persuasive to the Chamber given that the witness did not examine and did not treat the patient, and we're in the realm of conjecture as to the nature of the wounds and their possible effect upon the duration that life would continue after the wound. So we would not allow this question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have completed my cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Johan Tarculovski has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, Witness 171 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so that I'm certain, Your Honour, are we now in public session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Witness 171, could you please return to what was tab 13 in the binder provided you by my colleague. It's a photograph and this is Prosecution 65 ter 608. If that could be called up on our screen as well. If that could be blown up on the screen a bit, please. My colleague showed you this photograph a short time ago and asked you a few questions about it and you talked a bit about the nature of the wound, and possible consequences of this wound and bleeding, things like that. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you please look up to the area around the head of this body, please. If you take a look to what is the right side of the body's mouth, do you see what appears to be some blood on the right side of mouth on the cheek, coming out of the mouth to the cheek. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, there is something red there. I suppose it is blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then could you please look on the blanket that is next to the right side of the face, you see what appears to be some reddish material. It appears to be blood. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us, please, with this. Why would a person who receives a bullet wound like this in the abdomen or the stomach, why would this person also bleed from the mouth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Can I answer your question now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: If a patient is injured in the stomach, if the organ stomach is injured then they could vomit blood. But if they're injured in the lower part of the abdomen, then they would not vomit blood. So this vomiting could be a consequence of some other injury in the upper part of the body, in the mouth, the tongue, the teeth. Can you understand me? So the upper part of the abdomen, if that is injured, especially in the stomach is injured that could result there vomiting blood. Lower part of the abdomen injury would not cause vomiting blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You refer to vomiting blood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it possible that bleeding from the mouth is caused by internal bleeding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: It is like this. It can occur only if there is an injury of the intestines. In the upper part, it consists of the stomach and the duodenum and below that are the intestines, so it would be the position of the injury. This injury shown here in the photograph could not cause vomiting of blood. So an injury in the lower part of the abdomen, the injury of the lower intestines and internal bleeding, if a large blood vessel is injured, it is not connected to the lower intestines, so it could go out of the stomach or duodenum upwards, through the mouth. So it could be either an injury to the gastro-intestinal section which does not correspond to the actual position of this injury - I don't know what the actual post-mortem findings were - or it could only correspond to, the other possibility is it could correspond to an injury in the mouth or somewhere there. Because if there is a free discharge of blood inside the stomach it would remain -- in the abdomen, it would remain there. It would not go out through the mouth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And if the witness could be asked to speak slower then giving such expert testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could speak just a little bit slower, witness, then that would be helpful. Well, regardless of the cause of the bleeding of the mouth, of the bleeding from the mouth, would bleeding from the mouth also contribute to the death of the person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: If your question is as follows. If the mouth is injured, the interior of the mouth?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. If a person receives a gunshot wound that causes bleeding, people die from loss of blood; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if some of that loss of blood comes from the mouth, for whatever reason, would that loss of blood from the mouth also contribute to the death of the person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: So since we're discussing injuries from fire-arms, if there is a fire-arm injury to the stomach, and if the bleeding comes from the stomach then it is possible for the blood to be discharged through the mouth and also in the abdomen cavity, only when the stomach is injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have said that several times. That's very clear. My question was something different, very simple question. If someone bleeds from the mouth as well as other parts of their body, would the bleeding from the mouth also contribute to death. That's all. Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we call up, please, what was shown to the witness as 65 ter 1D454, please. This was tab 7 of the Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is, Witness, the report by Dr. Viktor Kamilovski dated the 14th of April, 2007. I want to explore one piece of this with you, please. Towards the bottom of the report it says the following. Actually, let me go a bit more slowly. Approximately, Witness, approximately in 2001 what percentage of the total population of Macedonia were ethnic Macedonians, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Around 20 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, maybe my question wasn't clear. I asked you what the percentage of ethnic Macedonians, persons who were ethnically Macedonian, what percentage would they be, would have been in 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Those who live in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. My question isn't clear so I'm going to try to ask it in a simpler way. Take a look at the line at the bottom here. It talks about out of 237 employees, 17 of them were members of ethnic minority groups. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In Macedonia in 2001, approximately what percentage of the population were made up of ethnic minority groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: If you're referring to the Albanian, I know that they were approximately around 20 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there are of course persons of Roma ethnicity, persons of Turkish ethnicity living in Macedonia as well, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that they would add a few more percentage points to the group of ethnic minorities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Well, if we work on the assumption that approximately -- there were approximately 23 per cent the population of Macedonia at that time were ethnic minorities, ethnic Albanians, Romas, Turks et cetera, you see in this line it says the employees of the hospital in 2001, 220 were Macedonian while the remaining 17 were members of ethnic minority groups. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we agree that 17 out of 237 is about seven per cent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so the remainder, the 220 ethnic Macedonian employees that would then, of course, be 93 per cent.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you think that ethnic minorities were well-represented at Skopje city hospital in 2001 amongst the employees and staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: I think they were well-represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we also see Prosecution Exhibit 192, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is at tab 1, Witness 171, of your binder, the Defence binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it not coming up on e-court? All right. I hope all the parties have a hard copy in front of them. I'll work with the hard copies for now. There it is. I apologise for moving my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My colleague, Witness 171, asked you some questions about this medical report. It is a report about Ismail Ramadani. And she asked you a question -- she asked you whether -- whether anything had been -- any information from the medical records for Mr. Ramadani had been concealed in this medical report and you responded no. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see anywhere in this medical report where it says, "hit by the police"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-171
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It is not written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we move into the private session, briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I indicate to you that that concludes the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber is very grateful that you have been able to come to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give to us. We thank you very much for that, and of course you may now return at a convenient time to your home and your work. So thank you indeed. We will adjourn now, and the court officer will then make arrangements. Did I interrupt you? You were about to saying something.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank you as well. And I was glad if I was able to assist the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, you call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness was already examined in chief and my learned colleague has started already his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. In those circumstances, may we welcome you back and remind you that the affirmation made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ali. You will recall that when we left off a few weeks ago I was asking you about the whereabouts of your brother, Vehap, on Friday, the 10th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in answer to my question, you explained that Vehap was at home. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And further in your testimony, you explained this. On Friday, when Erxhan was killed when I was informed at my uncle's house by phone, I went at my home, I found Vehap there at my father's house. This is transcript 2034. So your evidence, sir, at the time was that Vehap on Friday, the 10th, was at your father's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that Vehap had a house of his own. He did not live in the same house as his father Xhavit, there were two separate houses. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you have answered no. Perhaps I should ask the question better so that it can be clarified. Is that correct that Vehap had a house of his own in which he lived with his family?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he lived with his family. With the father and the whole family and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct that Xhavit, your father, had a house of his own?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In answer to a question that I asked you a few weeks ago about the people who had helped burying the body of your son, Erxhan, you answered that there was Fazil who is now dead, your uncle Avdil and yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that if someone were to claim that he and two other people but not yourself buried your son, that would be incorrect, right?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the person who said that was your father Xhavit, he would be wrong; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he said that, he was wrong. We were together with my father, with my uncles, with Fazil at home when we buried my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is 1D193. It has an ERN 1D002173. And in the Macedonian it would be 1D002181.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, what I wish to show you is again the statement of your father, Xhavit Ali, taken by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of October of 2004. And I will ask the registry to move to page 3 of that document. That would be 1D002175 in the English, and 2183 in the Macedonian. And if the registry could please focus on paragraph 9 of that page. Sir, I will read out to you what your father Xhavit said to the Office of the Prosecution, paragraph 9 of his statement: "On Friday, Saturday, until Sunday at 18 hours nobody dared to leave the basement of my house. Therefore we did not have any idea what was going on in the village. At about 1730, my brother's son Erhan Ali came to the basement carrying the dead body of Erxhan Ali. He was my grandson and Isni's son. The face was missing, his right hand was missing and there was hole in the right side of the ribs. Saturday was very quiet and in the evening we went out of the basement and buried the body of Erxhan in the yard of my house with Fasliu and Haki Rexhepi." Would you agree, sir, that this version given by your father is significantly different from yours?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Saturday, we buried Erxhan together in the afternoon. I don't know the exact hour. We were all there, my brother, my father, my uncles, Fasliu, cousins, we buried him and the shootings continued and we stayed in the basement until the next day at 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that your father makes no mention of your presence during that event; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you were asked a few weeks ago who was present during the burial, you did not mention your father; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. We were all together, the whole family at home. The uncles, the father, the brother. We were all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, going back to the Friday, the 10th of August, you explained that at the time the -- when the shelling started you went to Avdil's house and you found Avdil in that house. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Avdil was there Qamil Rexhepi was there and some -- some neighbours there were piling tobacco in the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall that this would be at around 4.00 or 5.00 in the afternoon, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's approximately the time when your son Erxhan was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that a fact, sir, that at the time when Erxhan was killed Avdil was not at his house but at the school in the village. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct that at that time there was a meeting between village leaders and a number of other individuals taking place in the school. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
