utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 1D92. It is 1D001296. And I believe there is no Macedonian version of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, the document which I would wish to show to you an is OTP statement of Mr. Kenan Saliu or Salievski. And first I should ask you do you know who Mr. Saliu or Salievski is?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know a Mr. Kenan Saliu living in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is he also known sometimes as Salievski, Kenan Salievski?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his last name. Kenan, yes, I know, he is a co-villager.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we could turn to page number 3 of Mr. Saliu's statement it is at 1D001298. And if the registry could focus on the middle of the page. There's a paragraph starting with the word: "The witness was standing." Mr. Ali, since there is no version in Albanian or Macedonian I will read the evidence to you. This is the evidence of Kenan Saliu. It says: "The witness was standing inside the school building together with Avdil Aliu, the uncle of Erxhan. Five or six other people were also present in the school. The witness remembers that his uncle got a phone call and some of his relatives said that Erxhan was killed. The call came to the telephone in the principal's office in the school building. The witness remembers the following people present in the school: Avdil Ali, Hysni Museli, Afet Zendeli, Nadim Musliu, Ramadan Nuredimi. Is that correct, sir, that at the time which you have indicated around 4.00, 5.00 on the 10th of August, Mr. Avdil Ali, your uncle was not his house but in the school building where a meeting was taking place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. And I would like to know who is playing these games. These things that you are putting to me are not correct. They've never been accurate. I don't know who is inventing all these lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that the purpose of the meeting was to discuss the defence of the village, how who organise the defence against a possible attack. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness has just answered but the witness himself was not at this meeting. He claimed to have been at home at this point in time, so the question is asking or inviting the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, there would be many other ways in which the information could have been acquired by the witness other than his presence at the meeting. We have no information to suggest that this particular witness was at the meeting. We understand that we have to put our case to the witness, and the meeting which took place at that time is relevant to this. It is also relevant to the credibility of this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Certainly insofar as you put a question that Avdil was not at his house, you certainly properly can. Where he may have been, you'll have to ask then whether the witness knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Ali, that armed men were patrolling the village in several locations in the village of Ljuboten on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. And I have arguments and facts that up to Friday, the Macedonian police could walk freely in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, also that the villagers who were present in this meeting were informed that NLA reinforcements would shortly be coming to the village. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't want to repeat my objection but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not correct. There was no NLA. Had there been NLA members, they wouldn't have been able to do that to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that during this meeting or shortly thereafter a number of villagers were distributed with live ammunitions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness answers I have twice object now against this line of questioning. The witness has said he was not at the meeting but at home and my learned colleague is putting again and again questions about the meeting and what happened after the meeting to the witness. Maybe as another line of questioning my learned colleague could ask whether the witness had later been at the school so that he establish some basis for his questions and for putting certain questions relating to the school to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question at the moment doesn't specify anything happening at the school but something happening, it could appear, village-wide. We do appreciate your concern, Mr. Neuner, that the question may be being directed contrary to the evidence of the witness. But we also appreciate Mr. Mettraux's position that he is needing to put a contrary position. As I understand it, that is what he is doing. And in that situation, he can put the position for which his client contends and the witness, as he clearly demonstrates he is capable of doing, will indicate his own understanding of what occurred, if he knows what occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, I will ask you the question once again. Are aware that during the meetings or shortly thereafter a number of villagers were distributed with live round of ammunitions?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no ammunition in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Moving on to Saturday, the 11th of August. You said in your statement that the shelling started again in the morning hours on Saturday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it started at around approximately 8.00 in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 8.00 in the morning, on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Ali, I'm now asking you questions if we can take one day back to Saturday, the 11th. Could you recall at what time approximately the shelling starting on that day, or what you have described as shelling.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling and shooting started, I don't know the exact time, but they lasted till noon. Then there was a lull and they re -- they continued the following day, on the Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that your evidence that the shelling and shooting was quite intense during that period? Was there a lot of shelling and shooting or was it sporadic?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting from light weapons and there was also shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in your view, sir, and to the extent that you can assess would that fire directed at the village, as you say, would this have been audible from the nearby village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were shooting from all sides. Our village is the only Albanian village in that area. They were shooting from all sides. We were in the basement and we could only hear the detonations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question was whether you are able to state whether that fire activity would have been audible from Ljubanci or not, if you are able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to, because I didn't dare to come out of the basement and look from which side they were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on Saturday, the 11th, sir, do you remember where your brother Vehap was at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was at home. On Saturday, in the afternoon, the shooting stopped, and that's when we buried my son together with my father, uncles, and cousins, all of us, 30 people were together in the basement, children, women, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, sir, so that it is clear for the record when you say he was at home do you mean by that that he was at his home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were together in one house at my father's house because my brother and I shared the same house as my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if your brother Vehap were to say that he was -- well, I withdraw that question, Your Honour. Do you know where Erhan, your cousin Erhan was on Saturday, the 11th?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Erhan, too, was in the house. We were all together in the house. My uncles, their wives, the children, all of us were in the basement. They had come on the occasion of my son being killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Ali, that during the weekend of the 10th to the 12th of August there were members of the NLA and armed civilians in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, have you been asked or told not to mention the presence of the NLA in the village during that weekend?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me or told me not to mention this. And the truth is that there was no NLA in the village. These are only lies, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that quite a number of villagers from Ljuboten had joined the ranks of the NLA in 2001? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell this Chamber who is Najl [phoen] Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Najl Ali is the son of my uncle on my father's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that would be your cousin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Najl was also the brother of Erhan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also that Najl Ali, your cousin, was a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war or before the war, he was staying with his uncles on his mother's side in Aracinovo. What happened later, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But my question was, sir, you are aware that your cousin, Najl, was a member of the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. Because personally I don't know this. He was staying with his uncles. We are simple villagers. We are always busy with our agricultural work so we see each other very rarely during the summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if his brother Erhan were to say that Najl was a member of the NLA you would not take any issue with that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could well say that, but I don't know this for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that correct, sir, that at the time of death of your son Erxhan, Rohan Jashari was present near or close by your son?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My son was on the street. When Erhan saw him killed, he took his body to the house. I don't know if there was anybody else there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Had Mr. Jashari joined the NLA, sir, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Jashari are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm referring to Ruhan or Rohan Jashari.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was at home. This I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, I think we must have been lost in the translation here. Could you confirm whether or not Rohan Jashari had joined the NLA at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because a day before the war started, I saw him in his house, because he is a neighbour. He lives very close by my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that members of the family of Mr. Rohan Jashari were members of the NLA, sir? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that Rohan's own brother was a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence, sir, is that you don't know whether members of Mr. Jashari's family and his own brother were in fact members of the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Rohan I guarantee you that he was not a member of the NLA. He was at his house. For the other person, I didn't see him, so I cannot guarantee anything about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to move on a little bit in time, Mr. Ali, to ask you what you describe as mistreatment and beating at the Prolece or Kisela Voda police station in Bit Pazar. Do you remember giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated, I believe, that the beating which you received had been quite severe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is your evidence that the injuries caused by those beatings remained apparent for several days or weeks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I still have a scar on my head. You can see it even nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated as well that while you were in the Prolece or Kisela Voda police station you were, as you said beaten on both hands by Kalashnikov butt rifle. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they performed the paraffin test they were hitting our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you tested positive to the nitrite particles after they carried out the paraffin glove test on you?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I was told. But when they carried out this test, my head was under the table. I don't know and I wasn't able to see what they were doing with my hands. I was just told that I tested positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you were asked to explain how the nitrite particles had come on to you? You recall being asked about that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall appearing in court in the month of October of 2001? I believe it was from the 24th to the 26th of October. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall being asked by the court or your lawyer being asked by the court to explain the presence of nitrite particles on yourself? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't asked about this in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this witness could be shown what is Prosecution Exhibit P50 with an ERN ET-N002-0285-1. The Macedonian version would be N002-0084-202. Well, that would not seem be to the correct document. I will repeat the ERN. It is ET N002-0285-1. And the Macedonian would be N002-0084-202. Thank you, yes, that is the correct document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask -- well, first perhaps going through that document, Mr. Ali. As you can see this is a decision or ruling depending on the translation, rendered by the Lower Court Skopje II. It seems like the Macedonian is not the same as the English version. Yes, the number of the Macedonian version would be N002-0084-202. Thank you. Sir, this is a ruling or decision of the Trial Chamber of the Lower Court, Skopje II, Skopje. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is dated the 26th of October of 2001. Can you see that? That is at the end of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we may turn, please, to the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be the third page in the Macedonian, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, there is a paragraph in this document which I wish to read to you. It says the following: "On 24th September 2001 the accused Ali Isni and Jatif Aliovski the village of Ljuboten, Skopje, stated their objection to the indictment, KO number 2801-01 of 7 September 2001, to the Trial Chamber of the Court through their Defence counsel, Petar Svetonov, an attorney-at-law of Skopje. Can you now recall this hearing, Mr. Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not asked about anything at this hearing. We only stayed ten minutes and then we were returned to the prison. Only the lawyers were asked questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall your lawyer being asked about the nitrite on yourself? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I continue reading from that paragraph. That would be the second page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the version from which I am reading is slightly different. It is two different translations, the same document having been admitted twice. We understand the substance is similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The decision or ruling -- this is not the correct page which is shown on the computer. It is ET-N002-0285-2. I'll continue, I'll read it for you for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may assist my learned colleague, I believe it is the second page of the B/C/S or of the Macedonian version. What is displayed on the right hand is the third page. I believe it is the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understand it is correct page in the Macedonian but the wrong page in the English, Your Honour, because they are two different translations, so it may be the third page in the English version, it is the second in ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, I apologise for the delay. I will read to you the paragraph in question. It says this: "In the objection submitted as well as in the session held on 25th October, 2001, in accordance with Article 261 paragraph 2 of the ZKP, where Petar Svetonov, attorney-at-law of Skopje, verbally explained the objection in the presence of the accused, stating that that accusation is based on only one piece of evidence, the paraffin glove test, which demonstrated the presence of nitrite particles, which evidence in and of itself, is insufficient for the crime of service in an enemy army. Since the accused fled arriving from a place which is contaminated due to the intensive events which took place there." Do you recall your lawyer making that objection, sir, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "In particular, he states that the accused Ali Isni had previous contact with a contaminated object, namely a piece of the shell with which his son Erxhan Ali was killed at the age of six years when struck on 10 August 2001." Can you remember your lawyer saying that?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This I remember, because I removed the shrapnels from the body of my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall your lawyer stating that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you -- you've just explained that you removed the piece of shrapnel in question. Did you take that piece of shrapnel with both of your hands or with one hand?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if I used both hands or one hand, but I just remember that I removed the shrapnel and when your child gets killed you don't pay attention to that. When I saw my son in pieces, I don't know how I can describe in words the feeling I was going through.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have just one more question, Your Honour, if you allow me to finish this part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Ali, that other villagers who had testified negative to nitrite were released on that date, including your brother Vehap. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The night we were brought there, they released my brother and some others. They told me brother to go, and they released whoever they wanted to. They said to my brother, "Choose who you want to come with you." He wanted me to go home as well, but they didn't let me go. There was not a -- there were releasing people at random.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that the truth, sir, that only those persons who tested positive to nitrite were kept in detention?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true, because around midnight we were removed from our room. We were taken to the corridor, we were told that we were going to be released. They lined us up there, they kept us there for 30 minutes and then they put us back in the room and told us that they could not release us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much Mr. Mettraux. We must adjourn now for the day and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. Before we do, although it is unusual, the Chamber understands that one of the accused has recently become a father. We congratulate him and his wife. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
